note: The competition is specified so that a lucky run cannot win it. Nothing is currently ranked, because no candidate has cleared a single admission gate. A blank board is the honest state, not a placeholder.

divisions.name: Singles
divisions.note: Settlement is the simplest to audit, which is why this division opens first.

divisions.name: Parlays
divisions.admission: G01, G03, G05, G06, G09 plus the singles gates for every leg
divisions.note: A parlay entry must satisfy every gate its legs satisfy, and must additionally show measured leg dependence.

divisions.name: Player props and prop combinations
divisions.unit: one player selection, or one explicit combination
divisions.admission: D-B plus a per-player usage sample
divisions.note: Player-level data is the weakest input here: this repository holds none.

divisions.name: Availability overlay
divisions.unit: one fixture, judged on how well the report-based adjustment predicted the game
divisions.admission: D-A plus several weeks of timestamped reports
divisions.note: Scored on prediction of the game outcome, not on whether a trade was profitable, so it can be evaluated before any price exists.

scoring.name: Skill score, not accuracy
scoring.rule: Entries are ranked by a proper scoring rule against the declared naive baseline (log score or Brier for probabilities, absolute error for totals). Hit rate alone is not scored, because it hides stake and price.
scoring.why: A 55% hit rate at a bad price loses money; ranking by hit rate rewards luck and punishes honesty.

scoring.name: Luck-adjusted interval
scoring.rule: Every entry is ranked with an interval that accounts for its number of independent events. Ranking uses the lower bound, not the point estimate.
scoring.why: Ranking on point estimates means the entry with the most variance can win a small sample by chance.

scoring.name: Declared trial count
scoring.rule: The number of variants each entrant tried is declared before scoring and the significance level is corrected for it.
scoring.why: Without this, the leaderboard rewards whoever searched hardest, not whoever found something real.

scoring.name: Frozen forward period
scoring.rule: An entry becomes eligible only after one full forward period with its rules frozen and untouched.
scoring.why: This is the only mechanism here that measures skill rather than fit.

scoring.name: Reproduction by a second party
scoring.rule: An independent rebuild from the committed snapshots must reproduce the entry's numbers exactly before it is ranked.
scoring.why: An unreproducible number cannot be checked for error, so it cannot be compared.

scoring.name: Withdrawal for unrealised claims
scoring.rule: Any claim of profit or edge without an executable, timestamped price is struck from the entry, not merely footnoted.
scoring.why: A claim that cannot be settled is not a result.

rewards.reward: Public listing in the division table with its evidence links
rewards.note: Non-monetary. No cash prize is funded, authorised, promised or implied anywhere in this project.

rewards.reward: Entry earns a rank in its division
rewards.note: Zero entries are qualified, so zero ranks exist.

rewards.reward: Independent reproduction badge, with the reproducing party named
rewards.note: Requires a second party. A self-reproduction does not qualify.

rewards.reward: Recorded in the season ledger, subject to the rights review in G01
rewards.note: Publication itself is conditional on G01 and G10, which are both currently blocked.

anti_luck_rules: No ranking from a single game, a single week, or any sample smaller than the pre-declared minimum.
No ranking of an entry whose price is unknown, because the return cannot be computed at all.
No 'best of N' display: every declared variant stays visible with its own result.
No mid-period rule change. A change resets the entry's forward clock to zero.
No reward is denominated in money unless a funded prize is separately documented; none is.
Ties are broken by the entry with the wider evidence base, not by the better point estimate.
